result:
This all looks correct and verified working. Here's a summary of what I found and fixed.

## What was actually wrong

This is Lumina, an AI meeting assistant, that pivoted from a previous product called InboxZap (an inbox-cleanup tool). The pivot broke SEO in several concrete ways:

1. **The homepage `<title>`/meta description still said "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes"** (`app/layout.tsx`), despite the homepage content being 100% about Lumina. That's actively misleading to both Google and searchers clicking through from search results.
2. **The blog was non-functional**: `/blog` was a client component fetching `/api/posts`, a route that doesn't exist (404 forever) — so the blog index rendered no content and linked to no posts. The 12 already-indexed blog URLs were orphaned, discoverable only by stale crawl memory.
3. **Those 12 indexed posts were about the old product** (inbox zero, bulk-deleting Gmail, unsubscribing from newsletters) — explaining the GSC pattern of huge impressions (40k+) but near-zero clicks at positions 40-65: thin/off-topic content for a business that no longer sells that.
4. **`/features` and `/pricing`** were linked in nav and listed in the sitemap but had no source files — a rebuild from this repo would have 404'd on both.
5. **`/faq` redirected to `/#faq`**, an anchor that didn't exist anywhere on the page.
6. **`sitemap.ts`** had a literal `TODO` and omitted blog posts, features, and pricing.

## What I changed

- Fixed root metadata to correctly describe Lumina (`app/layout.tsx`), added `metadataBase`.
- Added `app/features/page.tsx` and `app/pricing/page.tsx` as real source files.
- Rebuilt the blog as server-rendered (`app/blog/page.tsx`, new `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`) backed by `lib/posts.ts` — 6 new posts targeting keywords that actually fit the current product (meeting notes, action items, Zoom transcription, async recaps), each with proper per-page metadata and canonical tags.
- Added a 301 redirect for the old `/blog/post-1`..`post-12` URLs to `/blog` (`next.config.js`) instead of leaving already-indexed URLs to 404.
- Added an FAQ section to the homepage with an id for the existing `/faq` redirect to land on, including structured data (`FAQPage` JSON-LD) — and one FAQ entry explicitly addressing "Is Lumina the same as InboxZap?" to honestly capture that residual brand-search traffic instead of losing it.
- Updated `sitemap.ts` to include features, pricing, and all blog posts.

Verified with a full `next build` (clean, no errors/warnings) and a `next start` smoke test of every route: correct titles, working FAQ anchor, 301s on legacy post URLs, working blog navigation, and a complete sitemap.

Note: `npm install` surfaced that `next@14.2.5` has a known security vulnerability (patched in later 14.x releases) — unrelated to this task, but worth a separate upgrade pass. I didn't touch it here since it wasn't part of your ask and warrants its own regression testing.

Nothing has been committed — let me know if you'd like these changes committed.
